## Binding authority and spec reconciliation

Binding product ruling: https://github.com/division-sh/swarm/issues/2321#issuecomment-5577792999. It supersedes the original mock-default/graduation framing. `serve`, including `--dev`, is live; `test` is mock. Config cannot select posture. Agent `mock:` remains in source permanently and is consumed only in test execution. Retained serve defaults recovery to true; explicit false and dev scratch semantics remain. Existing store/workspace coordinates remain.

Read the full #2321 thread, #2319 body/thread and cross-pin, #2285 ownership ruling, and the implementer/semantic-drift guidelines. PR #2391 merged on 2026-09-07; its topology changes are present in the audited master.

Exact existing governing sections of `platform-spec.yaml`:

- `engine.process_execution_posture` (5898): currently requires authored posture and prohibits defaults. Its config/no-legacy text contradicts the new ruling and must be replaced, while causal-mode admission remains a real runtime invariant.
- `engine.agent_session_management.llm_provider_selection_config_authority.mock_agent_runtime` (6227), especially selection, lifecycle, fully-mocked startup waiver, authoring, and effect policy: currently mock presence selects mock even in a live process. Selection and waiver clauses must change together.
- `engine.boot_verification` (7816), `workspace_model.workspace_backend_selection` (19025), and source effect reachability: verification, credential, capability, and workspace consumers must follow the selected command execution.
- `configuration_source_authority.unified_swarm_config` source precedence/schema (18567 onward): retire the key in every layer, generated example/schema, diagnostic and config consumer. Keep other layer precedence under #1801.
- `engine.runtime_store_backend_selection` (5186) and `cli_specification.foundations.local_runtime_state_authority` (23109): preserve `.swarm/stores/dev.db`, separate `dev-scratch.db`, exact possession/epoch refusal, borrowed-source protection, and PostgreSQL selection.
- `test_specification.deterministic_scenario_runner` (20412), including `derived_scenario_compilation.execution_profile`, and `cli_specification.command_catalog.test` (23689): currently the CLI targets an existing server and explicitly does not activate mock execution. These are blocking contradictions with a command-owned mock runtime, not incidental documentation edits.
- Adjacent authority: API scenario selector admission, durable `run_scenario_execution_profiles`, source/effective-source identity, mock-effect denial, timer/readiness immutable execution mode, selected-contract and conversation fork ownership, provider-trigger credential admission.

No existing exact section defines a self-contained command-owned test runtime or structural readers under the new command split. The independent ruling now settles the product direction; Amendment 2 and the versioned spec delta supply the remaining concrete design for ratification. Authoritative platform-spec.yaml is NOT changed during this audit. Approved decisions must be promoted in the matching implementation PR.

## Classification, concept, and closure

- Category: semantic migration, execution-authority canonicalization, CLI/runtime/store parity, first-user conformance.
- Observed symptom: both newly generated archetypes fail bare `serve --dev` at store admission because the shipped hidden config explicitly chooses a SQLite path.
- Chosen working failure class: `command_owned_execution_and_zero_project_edit_startup`.
- Immediate parent: `execution_selection_admission_dispatch_authority_drift`.
- Broader parent: `deployment_and_test_authority_leaks_into_portable_source`.
- Exact concepts: command-owned live/mock selection; inert authored test doubles in live execution; selection-dependent startup and descriptor materialization; isolated mock scenario execution; deployment-only config and truthful provenance; retained recovery default; shipped-artifact and first-run ownership.
- Original issue framing: too narrow and now contradictory. The repaired body must encompass selection, test runtime ownership and all consuming families. A config deletion alone is not an honest closure.
- The observed store refusal and local defaults helper were entry points, not the audit boundary. Runtime, persistence, roots/continuations, forks, validation, CLI/API, and conformance producers were swept independently.
- Intended closure: **failure class eliminated**, conditional on gate approval and complete execution proof. This PR aims to eliminate its chosen working failure class entirely. No runtime closure is claimed now.

## Proposed architecture and decisions requiring the gate

### G1: command and process ownership

Propose one typed execution purpose passed by command composition into existing runtime construction: live serve versus mock test. Keep the existing internal `executionposture.Posture`/`executionmode.Mode` distinction and effect fences, but remove posture as an authored configuration input. Internal typed construction is not another user selector.

`swarm test` currently creates an API client (`test_command.go:331`), resolves `runtime.identity`, and publishes into its selected server. `operator_scenario_execution.go:76` rejects derived execution unless that server is mock-only. `operator_event_publish.go:655` takes root mode from the server. A local CLI variable cannot change any of these authorities.

Propose a command-owned isolated test runtime using existing serve/runtime/store construction and the existing scenario runner/public API handlers. Fresh temporary SQLite state, private loopback endpoint and token, no public exposure/channel registration/provider ingress, no project context/retained-store claim or current-context rewrite. Test cancellation/failure must join runtime work and close the selected store before releasing temporary resources. Concurrent live serve and test must not share agent identities through a store, ports, context registration, or scratch epoch. Backend parity harnesses use isolated PostgreSQL databases via the existing test provisioner; no new public posture/backend-test flag is proposed.

Independent ruling accepts fresh isolation and retirement of connected/ambient target selection, with a teaching refusal for explicit incompatible targeting. Amendment 2 supplies the concrete composition/lifetime for final review. Do not mutate a live server or ignore an explicit target. The existing scenario language, compiler, run profiles, public mutation/readback handlers and quiescence owner remain; no second runner or scenario framework.

Golden/lifecycle/catalog tests that currently launch `serve` with mock config are mandatory migration consumers. Their mock process/restart assertions move to the explicitly internal compiled harness defined in Amendment 2; they do not retain a public `serve` invocation claim. Separate real live command/restart proof remains mandatory. Do not relabel mock execution as live, create a hidden `serve --mock`, or substitute a unit simulator.

### G2: authored versus executable agent data

Propose that source retains the compiled test double as authored source data, while canonical selection produces the executable descriptor for the command. Live descriptors omit the inactive performance; test descriptors contain the exact compiled bytes/digest and mock mode. This preserves the current selected-store rule rejecting live descriptors that carry executable mock artifacts. Persistence consumes the resolved descriptor; it does not strip/reselect on read.

All static/template activation, reconfigure/replacement, recovery, restart, selected-contract execution and fork-chat must consume the same selector. Source mock presence may no longer waive live credentials, model, Claude CLI or native capability checks. Config or persisted `llm_backend: mock` must not become an alternative public command selector. Current historical causal mode must never be rewritten during recovery or fork; unsupported old selected stores remain unsupported, with no conversion or compatibility reader.

Proposed missing-performance scope: all effective agent declarations admitted into the test runtime, enumerated through scope-complete `semanticview.AgentDeclarations`, including templates/imports and duplicate local names. Missing performances fail before runtime/store/provider mutation with exact agent and `add mock:` guidance. Do not infer reachability from names or test coverage. Live execution retains source grammar validation of `mock:` but never executes it.

### G3: verify, backend, and environment prerequisites

Independent ruling accepts structural verify and describe without execution selection or live credentials; live startup readiness remains in serve/doctor, and test performs mock-specific completeness/effect admission. Amendment 2 classifies existing checks and output fields; no indiscriminate suppression.

The built-in backend default is Anthropic API (`selection.DefaultBackend`), unchanged by this work. The original audit incorrectly called Claude CLI the default; Claude is the operator-selected profile used for provisioned L proof. The independent ruling confirms genuine Claude/Docker/model prerequisites and honest installation guidance remain: zero project edits does not mean an unprovisioned machine. Do not change backend default or waive native/exec checks incidentally. No real external provider was invoked by this pre-implementation audit.

### G4: ingress dependency and deployment defaults

Credential-absence dormancy belongs to existing #2319, whose repaired body/thread carries the new ruling. F retains ownership; its proof blocks combined credential-absent webhook acceptance, not G's independent composition work after approval. No absorption, fake raw subscriber, dummy production signing key, broad credential waiver, or credential-as-posture selector.

Keep current config layering for unrelated facts (#1801). Reject retired posture at its actual file/key source even if another layer overrides it. Preserve valid deployment backend/secret references. Retire shipped `swarm.live.yaml` too. Recovery default true belongs to config resolution with presence-aware override semantics; an explicit false must survive merging. `--dev` remains fresh scratch.

## Full user-visible paths and gate classification

S = same chosen class; D = different semantic concept with named evidence; X = explicitly split/tracked.

1. `swarm new` -> exact embedded artifact inventory -> generated tree/next-command output [S]. Destination no-overwrite/file-copy semantics [D: `new_archetype.go`, retain existing scaffold refusal tests]. No generation of config or `.swarm/`.
2. Invocation root -> layered config/retired-key diagnostics/defaults [S for retired posture/defaults; X #1801 for unrelated discovery policy] -> exact source/resource loading [D: #2391 merged filesystem-tree loader and canonical-routing corpus; retain invalid source, symlink and missing-module proofs].
3. Bare verify -> source checks and classified deployment readiness [S, G3]. No config edit or hidden state creation should be required merely for structural verification.
4. Serve composition -> live selection [S] -> exact agent/model/capability/workspace projection [S selection consumers] -> backend prerequisites/secret resolution [S truthful reachability; D native/exec execution semantics, preserve negative proofs] -> ingress credential activation [X #2319] -> selected-store/epoch possession [D #2360; existing refusal test plus public first-run proof] -> recovery default and existing startup admission [S default; D topology and transaction algorithms] -> Manager/runtime readiness -> ingress/agent/activity side effects and public health [S actual selected mode].
5. Retained restart -> same admitted source/store -> selected descriptor reconstruction -> default-on recovery / explicit-false admission -> timers/deliveries/decision/activity continuation -> ready [S selector propagation; D immutable causal/lifecycle transaction owners]. Dev uses a fresh scratch epoch, not this replay path.
6. Test command -> exact source/scenario discovery and validation -> scope-complete mock admission -> isolated runtime/store/startup [S, G1] -> runtime identity/effective source/profile matching [S consumption; D exact digest algorithm] -> setup/new-run or derived publish -> root mock causality -> template/agent/node/connect dispatch -> timer/card/activity/connector-response settlement -> public diagnose/trace/entity assertions -> joined shutdown [S mode/ownership propagation; D scenario grammar and quiescence algorithms]. Missing mock or identity mismatch must fail before publishing or launching work.
7. Test while live serve exists -> distinct test ownership -> zero live-store/context/credential/transport changes -> independent shutdown [S]. Current CLI does not satisfy this path.

Earlier admission/config/source/model/store gates must succeed before any observable turn; tests cannot bypass them to claim the complete first-run journey.

Actual pre-audit execution:

- Built the real current-master binary with `go build -o /tmp/agent-g-2321-swarm ./cmd/swarm`.
- Ran `swarm new zero-agent-automation` and `swarm new webhook-responder` into separate fresh temporary roots. Both succeeded and taught explicit config commands.
- Ran bare `swarm serve --dev` in each untouched generated root. Both exited 3 with `cannot use authored or shared SQLite path` pointing to their generated `.swarm/swarm.db`; neither reached runtime readiness.
- The first attempt was correctly blocked by inherited test-only `SWARM_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN`; repeated production-shaped commands with only that test variable unset. No provider credentials were printed or live services invoked.
- Focused current-contract config/selection tests passed: `go test ./internal/runtime/llm/selection ./internal/config -run '^(TestResolveAgentExecutionSelection.*|TestProcessExecutionPostureIsMandatoryAndStrict)$' -count=1`. These confirm current contrary semantics, not target behavior.
- Focused current scaffold/default/epoch tests passed: `go test ./internal/cliapp -run '^(TestScaffoldAdmittedArchetypesAndTeachNextCommands|TestDevScratchEpochRejectsConfiguredSQLitePath|TestDefaultRuntimeConfig_DoesNotInferLLMBackendFromCredentials)$' -count=1`. They currently enforce the old scaffold/default behavior; a passing unit suite does not negate the two failing real first-run journeys.

## Amendment 2: bounded composition and structural-reader repair

This section supersedes open questions and ambiguous proof wording in G1/G3/M19 above, not their consumer census or full-class closure commitment. Code baseline remains `09eaf68345cfc24770ce3b5109efd0d49cd15196` (fresh `origin/master` fetch unchanged). Proposed authoritative changes are versioned in `issue-2321-spec-delta.yaml` beside this audit. That file is a review draft, not the authoritative spec and not merge-time proof.

### Concrete composition and lifetime

Existing seam: `cmd/swarm/main.go` injects `cliapp.ServeRunner` into `cliapp.Execute`. Proposed corresponding injected `TestSessionRunner` accepts an already admitted test request and a callback that runs the **existing** `scenarioRunner` once the private API is ready. `serveapp.RunTestSession` implements it. `cliapp` never imports `serveapp`. The callback receives only the private endpoint/auth and admitted source identity, not a store handle. The production binary exposes only `swarm test`, with no daemon, restart, mode or retained-test-store option.

Extract the reusable construction immediately below `serveapp.Run`, not another constructor: selected-store construction `buildStores`, schema admission, source projection, `buildServeRuntimeBundleContext` -> `runtime.NewRuntime`, source-set installation, `startServeRuntimeContexts`, public API handler construction and existing lifecycle supervisor remain the implementation owners. Both `Run` and `RunTestSession` consume this one construction. Names for the bounded extraction are proposed, not existing APIs: `buildRuntimeComposition`, `Start`, `WaitReady`, `Close`; they compose the existing functions and do not interpret run/agent/timer/recovery semantics. No general service framework or caller-pluggable semantic policies.

| Stage / resource | Public test owner and order | Failure / release responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Parse/admit (before acquisition) | CLI rejects explicitly set `--api-server`, `--context`, target-token options before connection resolution. Parse all discovered config layers, reject invalid/retired keys even when overridden, compile source/pack metadata and authored/derived scenarios, validate all admitted doubles and exact responses. | No HTTP request, credentials lookup, database opening, project claim, actor or listener on refusal. Config source selection remains supported; connected execution is retired. |
| Select execution inputs | Command fixes mock execution. Build a typed session request from admitted source/scenario facts, source model metadata and bounded timeout/output settings. Deployment DB/DSN/listener/token/public exposure/channel activation/current-context/workspace-root selections never enter it. | Syntactically/semantically invalid config is still rejected before this projection. Valid deployment settings do not select a server, open a DSN/token file, acquire a credential or choose test workspace location. No mutation of shared config to pretend it was absent. |
| Acquire fresh session | `RunTestSession` creates one private temporary root, SQLite database and workspace backing root per invocation; source artifact materialization remains read-only. Existing selected-store/schema/process-possession owners apply to these exact resources. | Register reverse-order cleanup immediately after each acquisition. No project retained/dev database, `.swarm` context record, user workspace backing or `current` pointer is acquired. Host-only isolated mock work uses existing embedded Python/WASI/effect fences; no Docker discovery or native execution waiver. |
| Bind/construct | Reserve ephemeral loopback listener(s), generate private transport auth in memory with the scopes the scenario runner needs, bind existing gateway/API and runtime context composition to them. Context registration is in-memory only. | No operator token file, credentials store, ambient server or public exposure. A listener may exist before readiness but mutation admission remains closed. If the existing gateway requires a loopback MCP listener, the session owns it too; it cannot resolve external MCP providers. |
| Start/readiness | Existing process supervisor and `startServeRuntimeContexts` own startup, topology/recovery ordering and producer release. Wait for existing committed readiness plus exact `runtime.identity`/effective source matching. | Startup failure cancels and joins every acquired runtime/context; never invoke scenario callback early. Public test mounts no provider ingress, channel registration or external activation. |
| Execute | Existing authored/derived scenario runner calls the private real API; exact profile installation, root mode, dispatch, diagnostics and quiescence stay with current owners. | Preserve timeout/error/exit classification. Mock response and external-effect denials remain fail-closed; no callback fallback into live execution. |
| Stop/close | On callback completion, failure or cancellation, withdraw readiness/admission, cancel owned work, drain/join via existing supervisor, shut down API/gateway HTTP workers, close contexts/workspaces and selected store, then release temp root. | Cleanup errors are surfaced, not success. Never remove files while workers still own them. Forced death cannot run cleanup: OS releases process/listeners, orphan private temp state is never selected on a later public test; no scavenger, recovery protocol or compatibility machinery is added. |

Internal retained proof is a different **lifetime**, not another execution selector: compile a `_test.go` subprocess entry (proposed `TestOwnedMockLifecycleProcessEntry`) in the composition package with `go test -c`. The parent test provisions and owns one isolated SQLite directory or PostgreSQL database and workspace root for the whole journey; passes exact coordinates and test transport/signing secrets to each child; starts, awaits readiness, gracefully stops or SIGKILLs and joins the child; reopens the same coordinates in a new child for J1-J4. Each child uses the same construction/selection/possession/startup/API/effect owners. For fresh-epoch J5 it exercises the existing scratch epoch admission/replacement owner, not hand deletion of selected rows. Parent cleanup closes children before releasing roots or dropping the isolated test DB. There is no arbitrary existing-store input on a public command.

Only this internal harness mounts an explicitly local authenticated ingress fixture: an ephemeral loopback listener and fixture-owned signing credential feed the real inbound authentication, standing targeting, receipt, normalization, settlement and delivery owners. No normalized-event injection replaces signed requests. No external registration or tunnel is opened. Test HTTP auth and fixture signing secret are transport fixtures, not live-provider credentials. Invalid signatures, absent signing credential and transport failure must retain their real refusal semantics. Mock causality still forbids outbound transport. This fixture permission is compiled into the test entry, not a flag/env switch understood by the production binary. Lifecycle fixtures preserve real source, store, admission and causal gates; validation-only harness boundaries are not silently added to their source.

Required new L test is `TestCommandLiveServeAndRestartParity` (planned): build release binary; for each store run a source that retains doubles using a supported configured live backend, verify a real live turn/readback; gracefully restart and force-kill/restart retained state with omitted recovery; send authenticated ingress and assert exact route/convergence; separately run dev twice with durable sentinel untouched. Provider/auth prerequisites are provisioned through legitimate machine/deployment interfaces, not source edits. Absence is a recorded closure blocker. Required T tests include authored, derived, explicit-target rejection and live concurrent sentinel isolation. H covers retained mock lifecycle, not a public test restart feature.

### Structural-reader owner and check/output classification

Observed additional consumers: both `runDescribeCommandWithOutput` and `runDescribeRoutesCommandWithOutput` load the bundle then call `bootverify.Run` on the unprojected wrapper. Main describe also calls `resolveWorkspaceBackendDiagnostic`; verify currently calls that mock-sensitive classifier, opens credential owners, then `AdmitEffectiveSourceProjection`. These paths move to the same existing source/pack metadata admission and effective-source projection, then the structural portion of existing workflow validation/bootcheck owners. Render authoring/routing views from that admitted source with one report. Do not independently synthesize provider event schemas in describe. Runtime serves that source only after its separate live admission.

| Check owner / existing IDs or gate | Structural validity (verify/describe/routes and shared admission) | Test completeness | Live readiness (serve/doctor) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bootCheckRegistry` and `supplementalChecks` in `bootverify/checks.go` | All checks except the explicit runtime-dependent portions below remain, including every event/pin/flow/entity/loop/timer/schema/scope/permission/lint/metadata check. Keep existing severity and provenance; do not drop checks by blanket error filtering. | Same structural checks first | Same structural checks first |
| `credential_key_exists`, emitted `managed_credential_state`, provider credential snapshots | Declaration/reference syntax remains with source loaders; no store construction/read or credential-state finding | No live credential admission; exact authored doubles/responses instead | Existing static/managed/provider required-key and state checks over live effect reachability; #2319 narrows ingress absence only |
| `mcp_server_reachable` and concrete MCP discovery | No network/process probes | No discovery or external MCP use | Probe required configured servers; fail under existing readiness policy |
| `tool_resolution`, `required_mcp_tool_availability`, `platform_tool_usage_hints` | Preserve exact declared tool candidate/permission/reference/usage/schema checks using declared metadata; do not call `mcpDiscovered` or invent discovered success | Existing mock effect restrictions; source requirement remains visible | Additionally verify concrete MCP capability and tool fulfillability. Refactor mixed check internals in existing owner, never suppress the entire ID |
| `invalid_field_detection` / `validateAgentModelSelection` | Keep field and model declaration grammar, authored backend validity, alias syntax and explicit source references; no execution choice from mock presence | Live pin plus double legal; retain live model metadata while selecting exact double | Resolve configured live provider/model/alias support via canonical selection; missing environment/provider capability fails here |
| `native_tools_valid`, `workspace_class_exists`, `agent_permission_validation`, generated tool closure | Keep supported native declaration, permission, workspace class and source schema checks | No actual native execution; existing mock-effect fences reject it | Concrete native/exec/Claude/workspace/backend requirements still enforced by typed reachability/preflight |
| `PrepareSourceBootEffectContext` and connector mock-response admission | Validate supplied mock artifact/response grammar, exact references and schema; missing double/response is not structural invalidity | Require every effective agent double and each required exact connector response before resources/dispatch; existing response owner is canonical | Doubles inert; live backend/model/credential readiness cannot be waived by their presence |
| `ValidateWorkflowContractSurface` post-boot gates | Keep harness-boundary classification, tool implementation declarations, emit/generated schemas, durable activity surface, provider/channel/standing declaration grammar, pack compatibility and authentication declarations | Enforce selected mock performance and response requirements | Acquire activation/credentials/runtime resources only here; no structural report pretending to attest deployment |

The denominator is **all** current `bootCheckRegistry`/`supplementalChecks` entries plus post-boot gates in `workflow_validation.go`, not selected warning strings. Planned `TestStructuralCheckPurposeCensus` enumerates registrations, requires explicit structural/live/mixed classification, and fails on an unclassified new ID. Mixed IDs are separated at their existing producer, not reinterpreted by CLI output readers. Include invalid source, missing declared workspace/tool, malformed supplied mock, missing mock and unavailable live resources as distinct negative test cases.

| Existing output field/family | Amendment decision |
|---|---|
| verify `ok`, errors/warnings/lint_evidence and finding check_id/severity/location/message/remediation/evidence | Report structural result only, preserve severity/location; add explicit `validation_scope: structural` and `live_readiness: not_evaluated` to verify/describe results and matching human teaching. No skipped-probe success finding. |
| `production_valid`, harness counts and input/output provenance | Keep current no-validation-only-harness-dependence meaning exactly. `production_valid: true` is not credentials/model/machine ready. Human output explains this boundary. |
| verify/describe `workspace_backend` string | Remove mock-sensitive backend decision from structural results, with no compatibility alias. No deployment preview is needed in bare readers; doctor/serve keep actual live backend/reasons. This is a deliberate pre-1.0 output change. |
| verify `capability_subjects`, `pack_inventory` | Retire `capability_subjects` from the structural verify result: its `packs.Subject` includes required READY/NOT_READY/AVAILABLE status and operational credential/admission observations, so returning it without observation would be misleading. Keep `pack_inventory` and declared source capability validation; describe retains declared ingress/events/requirements. Doctor/serve and their existing operational capability projections remain unchanged. No compatibility alias or new capability-status algebra is introduced. |
| describe View (source_hash/source_authority, root, flows, approval_points, stage_graphs, routing_topology, diagnostics, equivalence) | Preserve projection meaning and canonical source identity. All diagrams, graph and JSON/quiet routes derive from the same admitted source/report. No inferred live backend from source mock. |
| `describe routes` routing-topology/v1 edges/issues/root inputs | Keep schema and stable quiet IDs; source admission must match verify/describe. No live readiness meaning added to topology issues. |
| health/subscriptions/runtime identity, doctor and serve boot announcements | Remain actual process/live readiness observations; causal mock mode remains visible on test API. These do not consume a fabricated structural readiness result. |
